content.text:
The native Effect and Alchemy work is merged into main and live on Production at `taxkit.dev` and `api.taxkit.dev`, and the public and browser checks pass.

**Main and PRs**
- [crcorbett/taxkit#173](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/173): the main change (`c6c4d892`).
- [crcorbett/taxkit#174](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/174): a deploy fix found on Preview (`4cb91fb8`). Alchemy's check for whether the Website needs rebuilding was following linked `node_modules` and reading about 1.2 million files. One Preview deploy stalled for six minutes and the next ran out of memory. With the fix, deploys take about 30 seconds.
- [crcorbett/taxkit#175](https://github.com/crcorbett/taxkit/pull/175): records the delivery and limits in the active plan (`a09b20f6`, docs only).
- Production runs `4cb91fb8`. The original checkout at `/Users/cooper/Projects/taxkit` wasn't touched.

**Checks before merging**
- `bun run verification` passed: build, format, lint, types, Effect diagnostics, every package's tests, browser tests, knip, docs and repository paths.
- `bun run test:native` passed: 11 files, 22 tests on the local Website/API pair.
- Changesets resolve.
- GitHub Actions were not relied on.

**Deployment**
- I deployed locally with native Alchemy and Doppler: Preview `pr-173` first, then Production at 04:32 UTC.
- The Production plan left the zone and DNS settings unchanged.
- The Preview is destroyed, and its addresses now return 404.

**Public and browser results (Production)**
- **Redirects:** `www` returns 301 and keeps the path and query.
- **Caching:**
  - A docs page's HTML and Markdown at the same address are both cached after the first request, whichever comes first.
  - An unrelated cookie doesn't stop HTML being shared.
  - API reads with and without an `Origin` are cached separately.
  - Calculations, errors and health checks are never cached.
- **Discovery files:** robots, the sitemap and llms point to `https://taxkit.dev`.
- **Cross-origin access:** any HTTPS site can call the API without credentials. MCP accepts browser calls only from `https://taxkit.dev` and still accepts clients that send no origin. `/_serverFn` returns 404.
- **Calculations:** $1,654 weekly gives $1,301.00 take-home both without JavaScript and in the browser. The browser calls `api.taxkit.dev` directly, and docs navigation makes exactly two API calls with no console errors.
- **Content refresh (Preview):** a content-only edit reached the API JSON, the page HTML and the Markdown. I then restored it.
- **Cache bug from the Site session:** TaxKit isn't affected, and I've sent that session the hosted evidence.

**Rollback**

Redeploy `f2191048` with that revision's own commands.

**Remaining limits**
- **Drift report:** `production:drift` reports both Workers as changed straight after a clean deploy, without naming fields. `production:plan` shows no changes and Preview shows no drift, so I didn't repair anything.
- **Failed page status:** server page loads that fail return 500 rather than the 503 the code sets, because TanStack overrides it. They're still `no-store`.

content.text:
The Site session was right: TaxKit Production is affected by the uncacheable-reply case. I warmed `taxkit.dev/sdk/effect-sdk` to a HIT, then sent an odd `Accept` header, which returned a `no-store` 400/406. The next plain request was a MISS, so the cached page had been evicted.

I've written the fix on branch `claude/taxkit-negotiation-cache`; it isn't committed or deployed yet:
- **The fix:** a 400 or 406 that varies on `Accept` is now stored as its own public cache variant. Missing (404) and unavailable (503) replies stay `no-store`. The API's own 400s vary on `Origin`, not `Accept`, so they stay `no-store` too.
- **Checks so far:**

  | Check | Result |
  | --- | --- |
  | api-http tests (one new) | 47 pass |
  | web unit tests | 85 pass |
  | native pair suite, updated to expect public caching on these answers | 22 pass |
  | types, lint and docs check | clean |

- **Docs and changeset:** the Website and api-http READMEs are updated, and a patch Changeset is added.

Full `bun run verification` is running. When it passes I'll commit, merge, deploy Preview, then Production. On each I'll check that the page stays a HIT after an odd-`Accept` request, then report back to the Site session.

content.text:
Mostly yes, with one real gap: Production is also still served on the `workers.dev` addresses.

**What matches Common Practice:**
- The www redirect uses Alchemy's own `domain.redirects`, with no Worker or ASSETS workaround. On Production, `www.taxkit.dev` returns a 301 that keeps the path and query.
- The zone is adopted and retained, and nothing outside Production gets a custom domain.
- Both repositories share the beta.81 limit when a ruleset read fails, which I've recorded.
- TaxKit passes `zoneId` explicitly while Common Practice leaves it out. Common Practice only omits it because its hostnames are spread across two zones. TaxKit has one zone, so that difference is harmless.

**Where TaxKit differs:**
1. **`workers.dev` stays on in every stage.** `apps-stack.ts` sets `workersDev: true` on both Workers, so it stays on in Production. Both Production Workers still answer on their `workers.dev` addresses (I just got 200 from each), and every deploy also gets a version preview address. Common Practice turns the Website's `workers.dev` off in Production and leaves preview addresses off in the other stages. Nothing in TaxKit relies on the Production `workers.dev` addresses; the Website reaches the API through a private service binding.
2. **Fewer zone settings managed in code.** Common Practice also manages zone settings (TLS, HTTPS), DNSSEC and the bot policy as retained resources. TaxKit only keeps its existing DNS settings. That isn't about www, but it is the rest of Common Practice's native DNS setup.

I recommend fixing the first point to match Common Practice: no `workers.dev` for the Website in Production, and no preview addresses anywhere. The API keeps its `workers.dev` address, as in Common Practice. I'd fold that into the cache-fix PR I'm about to merge and deploy. It removes a public address from Production, so I'm checking with you first.

The second point is a bigger change to live zone settings, so I'd leave it for a separate change unless you want it now.
